mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with offsetting housing demand, resulting in neutral to slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to lower corporate profit margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.0% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC is below 0.06.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a softening economic cycle and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous 6-month average AND GDPC1 < previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC is below 0.08.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the CPIAUCSL index above 4% on a year-over-year basis signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to consider tightening policy, which raises interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC is below 0.07.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals a significant labor market shock, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 6-month averages signals a broad-based recovery in demand and supply, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous 6-month average AND INDPRO > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC is below 0.10.
